questions.q: What does { FIXED [Customer Name] : MIN([Order Date]) } compute?
options: Each customer's earliest order date, stable regardless of the current view
The most recent order date across all customers
The average number of days between a customer's orders
The date the workbook was last refreshed
questions.explain: FIXED locks MIN([Order Date]) to the Customer Name grain, giving each customer's first purchase date independent of whatever's on the view — the foundation for both the new-vs-returning flag and the cohort grouping in this lesson.

questions.q: Why does the New vs. Returning flag (IF [Order Date] = [Customer First Order Date] THEN "New" ELSE "Returning" END) require a FIXED LOD expression rather than a plain date comparison?
options: Because Customer First Order Date must stay the customer's absolute earliest date regardless of the view, which only a FIXED expression can guarantee
Because Tableau requires all IF statements to reference an LOD expression
It doesn't actually require FIXED — any calculation would work identically
Because dates cannot be compared directly in Tableau without an LOD expression
questions.explain: Without FIXED, a reference to 'first order date' would only reflect whatever's visible in the current view, not the customer's true full-history first order — which defeats the purpose of a new-vs-returning flag.

questions.q: What does DATETRUNC('month', [Customer First Order Date]) produce, and why is it useful here?
options: A 'Cohort Month' field that rounds each customer's first purchase date down to the start of its month, grouping customers by acquisition period
The exact day of the customer's first order, unchanged
A count of how many months the customer has been active
The current month, regardless of the customer's actual first order date
questions.explain: DATETRUNC rounds a date down to the start of the specified period. Applied to the FIXED first-order date, it groups every customer whose first purchase fell in the same month into one cohort.

questions.q: In the suggested lab view (Cohort Month on Rows, AVG(Customer Lifetime Sales) on Columns, New vs. Returning filtered to 'New' only), why filter to 'New' only?
options: So each customer is counted exactly once, at their first order, rather than once per order they've ever placed
Because 'Returning' customers have no lifetime sales value
Filtering to 'New' has no effect on the result — it's purely cosmetic
Because Cohort Month only exists for new customers
questions.explain: Without that filter, a customer's row would appear once per order, and averaging Customer Lifetime Sales across those repeated rows would overweight customers with more orders. Filtering to New keeps one row per customer.

questions.q: What are the two FIXED LOD expressions this lesson builds the entire analysis on top of?
options: { FIXED [Customer Name] : SUM([Sales]) } and { FIXED [Customer Name] : MIN([Order Date]) }
{ INCLUDE [Order ID] : COUNTD([Product Name]) } and { EXCLUDE [Sub-Category] : SUM([Sales]) }
RUNNING_SUM(SUM([Sales])) and RANK(SUM([Sales]))
{ FIXED : AVG([Sales]) } and { FIXED [Region] : SUM([Sales]) }
questions.explain: Customer Lifetime Sales and Customer First Order Date — both FIXED to Customer Name — are the two building blocks every other field in this lesson (New vs. Returning, Cohort Month) derives from.
